web.settings.background.footer: Your device works through these by itself and pauses while you upload. You can keep using it meanwhile.
web.settings.background.title: Background work
web.settings.bridge.enable_failed: Could not switch the bridge on.
web.settings.bridge.intro: This device is only reachable on your home network. Through the {bridge} bridge it gets its own address, so you can reach it from anywhere and add friends. You'll need an Off The Cloud account.
web.settings.bridge.leave_confirm: Take this device off the bridge? {domain} is given back and the device restarts. It keeps everything on it and works at home, at {address}, but is no longer reachable from outside or by your friends. You can join again later.
web.settings.bridge.leave_hint: Leaving the bridge gives the name back; the device keeps working at home. To delete your Off The Cloud account as well, leave first, then use <account>your account page</account>. What the bridge keeps about you is in the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy>.
web.settings.bridge.name: Device name
web.settings.bridge.name_hint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. A name your account already holds moves to this device.
web.settings.bridge.pending_join: Joining {bridge}… the device restarts to finish, which takes about a minute. You may need to sign in again afterwards.
web.settings.bridge.pending_leave: Leaving {bridge}… the device restarts, which takes about a minute. From then on open it at home, at <link>{address}</link>.
web.settings.bridge.released: This device left the bridge: {bridge} no longer knew its name (its account was deleted, or the name released). Everything on it is still here.
web.settings.bridge.setup_hint: No account yet, or you sign in another way? Create one or sign in at <account>{address}</account>, choose “Get a setup code” and paste it here. See the <terms>terms</terms> and the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy>.
web.settings.bridge.title: Bridge access
web.settings.faces.hint: Detect faces in newly uploaded photos so you can search by person, like other photo apps. Off unless you turn it on (here or during setup), and faces never leave the device. It looks at everyone in your photos, not just you. It only affects photos uploaded while it is on — use Reprocess Media to scan the ones you already have.
web.settings.faces.title: Face Recognition
web.settings.language.changed: Another app changed the language at the same time. This browser now uses that one.
web.settings.language.hint: Every app signed in to this device uses this language. Automatic follows the language of each browser, phone or computer.
web.settings.language.not_saved: Couldn't save it on your device. This browser will try again when it reconnects.
web.settings.language.title: Language
web.settings.language.too_old: This browser will remember it. Update your device to use it in every app.
web.settings.logs.hint: What the device is doing, live - useful when something goes wrong. You can copy them, or send them to us so we can help.
web.settings.logs.send_hint: Sends the last part of your device's logs, your note and your account's email to info@off-the.cloud, so we can help.
web.settings.logs.sent: Sent - we'll answer at your account's email.
web.settings.logs.title: Logs
web.settings.logs.warning: Logs can include file and folder names, search words, Wi-Fi network names and your device's addresses. Check them before you share them.
web.settings.memories.hint: Photos taken around today in earlier years, at the top of Images. To choose the best ones, the device measures how each photo looks (its sharpness, its exposure and a quality score), on the device itself.
web.settings.memories.title: Memories
web.settings.notifications.hint: Get a push notification in this browser when a friend posts. Self-hosted — this device sends it directly, no third-party notification service involved.
web.settings.notifications.title: Notifications
web.settings.password.title: Change Password
web.settings.places.hint: Show your photos and videos on a map, at the places they were taken. Off unless you turn it on. While it is on, the device reads where each one was taken from its location data and keeps those locations unencrypted, so the map opens quickly. Turning it off deletes them. The map itself comes from a map service, which sees the area you look at but never your photos.
web.settings.places.title: Places
web.settings.profile.title: Profile
web.settings.reprocess.confirm_restart: Reprocess every photo and video in your library? This deletes all existing tags and recognized people and rebuilds them from scratch. It can take a while and can't be undone.
web.settings.reprocess.confirm_resume: Resume reprocessing where it left off? It can take a while.

web.settings.reprocess.failed.one: Last run failed after {count} file(s) — try again.
web.settings.reprocess.failed.other: Last run failed after {count} file(s) — try again.

web.settings.reprocess.hint: Re-run tagging and face detection on every photo and video already in your library — useful after a detection fix or model update. This clears existing tags and recognized people first and rebuilds them from scratch.
web.settings.reprocess.title: Reprocess Media
web.settings.restart.confirm: Restart the device? It will be unreachable for about a minute.
web.settings.restart.needs_update: Your device needs an update before it can be restarted from here.
web.settings.restart.slow: The device hasn't come back yet. It can take a little longer; if it doesn't come back, unplug it and plug it back in.
web.settings.restart.wait: Restarting… the device will be back in about a minute.
web.settings.session.hint: This browser stays signed in across reloads. Sign out if you're on a shared or public computer.
web.settings.session.title: Session
web.settings.smart_search.download_note: Turning it on the first time downloads about 400 MB to your device.
web.settings.smart_search.hint: Find photos by describing them, in any of the app's languages. Your device works this out itself and keeps it encrypted. Turning it off deletes what it learned.
web.settings.smart_search.off_text: Your device deletes what it learned about your photos. Turned on again, it has to look at all of them again, which takes a while.
web.settings.smart_search.title: Smart search
web.settings.social.hint: Photos and videos from your friends' posts are kept on this device, so your feed works even when they're offline. When they take more than this, the oldest friends' posts are removed. Your own posts and files are never touched.
web.settings.social.saved: Saved. Older posts over the limit are being removed.
web.settings.social.title: Friends' posts storage
web.settings.social.too_small: Enter a size of at least 0.1 GB.
web.settings.storage.adding: Erasing ⁨{disk}⁩ and adding it to the mirror…
web.settings.storage.confirm_text: Everything on ⁨{disk}⁩ will be erased: all its files and partitions, for good. It then becomes the mirror's second disk, and the device copies all your files onto it.
web.settings.storage.confirm_title: Erase this disk and use it for the mirror?
web.settings.storage.copying: ⁨{disk}⁩ is now the mirror's second disk. The device is copying all your files onto it, which can take hours; the device can be used meanwhile.
web.settings.storage.failed: The disk could not be used for the mirror.
web.settings.storage.look_alike: Another disk plugged in looks just like this one, so neither can be chosen here: unplug the one to keep first.
web.settings.storage.new_disk: New disk found: ⁨{disk}⁩. It has data on it, so it wasn't added to the mirror.
web.settings.storage.not_added: ⁨{disk}⁩ wasn't added to the mirror. Alerts says why.
web.settings.storage.title: Storage
web.settings.tagging.hint: Recognise what newly uploaded photos and videos show (a beach, a dog, a birthday cake) so you can search for it. It runs on this device and nothing leaves it. Turning it off saves processing time; places from a photo's own location data are still searchable. It only affects what is uploaded while it is off.
web.settings.tagging.title: Image Tagging
web.settings.tailscale.authorise: Authorise this device in Tailscale, then press Enable again.
web.settings.tailscale.authorise_window: Authorise this device in the window that just opened, then press Enable again.
web.settings.tailscale.done: Done — this device is reachable at {address}
web.settings.tailscale.intro: Tailscale Funnel is an alternative to the Off The Cloud bridge, it publishes this device on your own ts.net address but with the next limitations:
web.settings.tailscale.key_hint: With a key from your Tailscale admin console this finishes on its own. Without one, you'll be taken to Tailscale to authorise this device.
web.settings.tailscale.limit_account: You'll need a Tailscale account, with Funnel enabled for your tailnet.
web.settings.tailscale.limit_one_user: One user only. Extra users need a web address each, and Funnel gives this machine a single one.
web.settings.tailscale.limit_social: The social side won't work. Friends find each other through the bridge, so sharing and friends' timelines are unavailable.
web.settings.tailscale.limit_traffic: Tailscale caps how much traffic can pass through Funnel, and doesn't publish the limit.
web.settings.tailscale.no_funnel: Tailscale is connected, but Funnel didn't come up. Check that Funnel is enabled for your tailnet.
web.settings.tailscale.not_installed: Tailscale isn't installed on this device, so Funnel isn't available here.
web.settings.tailscale.not_installed_ena: Tailscale isn't installed on this device, so Funnel can't be turned on here.
web.settings.tailscale.off: Funnel is off. This device is reachable through the bridge again.
web.settings.tailscale.popup_blocked: Your browser blocked the window — <link>authorise this device in Tailscale</link> instead.
web.settings.tailscale.suits: It suits a device you want purely as your own private NAS — your files and photos, reachable from anywhere, nothing shared with anyone.
web.settings.update.restarts_note: The device rebuilds itself and restarts, which takes a few minutes and drops this connection on the way. Your photos and settings are left alone.
web.settings.update.server_unreachable: Couldn't reach the update server just now, so this may be out of date.
web.settings.update.title: Device version
web.settings.users.created_no_password: User "{name}" created. This device doesn't set passwords yet, so {name} chooses one at the first sign-in. Update the device to choose it here next time.
web.settings.users.delete_confirm: Delete {name}? This permanently removes its database and every file it stored. Type {name} to confirm.
web.settings.users.hint: Each user runs as its own fully separate instance — own port, own database, own storage — managed only from here.
web.settings.users.local_hint: Uncheck to keep this account on your own network only — no remote access, and no friends outside your home.
web.settings.users.password_hint: Give it to {name} to sign in with. They can change it in Settings › Change Password, and from then on nobody else knows it.
web.settings.users.reachable_own: Reachable from anywhere at their own subdomain.
web.settings.users.title: Users
web.settings.wifi.confirm: Connect the device to ⁨{ssid}⁩? It leaves its current network and may not answer for about a minute. If the new network doesn't work, it goes back to the current one.
web.settings.wifi.confirm_cable: Connect the device to ⁨{ssid}⁩? It stays reachable through its cable while it does.
web.settings.wifi.intro: The network the device uses. Changed your Wi-Fi's name or password? Choose the network here and enter its password. If the device can't reach your Wi-Fi any more, connect it to your router with an Ethernet cable first.
web.settings.wifi.joining: Connecting to ⁨{ssid}⁩… The device may not answer for about a minute.
web.settings.wifi.name: Network name
web.settings.wifi.name_too_long: That name is too long: a Wi-Fi network name has at most 32 characters, and accented letters and emoji count as two or more.
web.settings.wifi.no_networks: No networks found. Scan again, or choose Other Network to type its name.
web.settings.wifi.password_invalid: A Wi-Fi password has 8 to 63 characters (accented letters and some symbols count as two or three), or exactly 64 hexadecimal digits.
web.settings.wifi.scan_failed: Could not look for networks. Try again.
web.settings.wifi.slow: The device hasn't answered yet. If it doesn't come back, connect it to your router with an Ethernet cable and open Settings › Wi-Fi again.
web.settings.wifi.title: Wi-Fi
web.settings.wifi.unknown_result: The device didn't say how the change went. The network it is on now is shown above.
